subject.title: refactor(qqbot): install plugin from Tencent package

question: Should OpenClaw approve @tencent-connect/openclaw-qqbot@2.0.0 as the official trusted QQBot runtime before it reaches SecretRef parity and has a proven existing-user upgrade path?
rationale: Merging changes the trusted code owner and package artifact while intentionally breaking a supported credential form, so automation cannot decide whether that security and compatibility boundary is acceptable.

options.title: Require parity before handoff
options.body: Hold the merge until the external package supports structured SecretRefs, docs and upgrade recovery are updated, and security verifies the exact pinned artifact.

options.title: Keep QQBot bundled temporarily
options.body: Retain the monorepo plugin until Tencent publishes a source-traceable, contract-compatible release that can replace it without user migration.

options.title: Accept the breaking migration
options.body: Approve the package and require explicit upgrade warnings and migration instructions for SecretRef and existing bundled-plugin users.

recommendation.title: Require parity before handoff
recommendation.body: Hold the merge until the external package supports structured SecretRefs, docs and upgrade recovery are updated, and security verifies the exact pinned artifact.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice concerns trusted plugin installation, package provenance, credentials, and host security rather than ordinary QQBot implementation details.
